structs.notes: Answer to the question. DWServicesAccess::GetInstance returns the address of the OnlineMgr singleton (lea rax, 0x14C3851A0; ret). The same address is the this of the OnlineMgr_*, Live_*, CL_Mgr_*, Com_* and LUI_* callers and of the dynamic initializers and the atexit destructor (dynamic_atexit_destructor_for_g_onlineMgr@0x142349640 calls OnlineMgr_ClearInstances on it). So the DW accessor is NOT a subobject at OnlineMgr+1880 in Replay: its methods receive the base with no adjustment. Replay has one local client (CL_Mgr_GetControllerFromClient@0x140D66C50 scans a single-DWORD table, from +0x72118 to +0x7211C), so the DW per-controller array has one live element. Blocker, left for the coordinator: DW methods read element 0 fields at base+16/+208/+424/+904 with stride 1136 and a count at base+1136, while ResetAllFences reads an OnlineErrorManager at base+8 out to base+1736. Both cannot be inline members of the same object. The tail (+24456, +24464, +24472) is solid and matches OnlineMgr_Init. DWServicesAccess (A096/A120 territory) should be told: no +1880 subobject in Replay; its size is still unproven. The global name g_onlineMgr is on the wrong address: the dynamic initializer and atexit destructor work on 0x14C3851A0 (the object), so g_onlineMgr belongs there, and the IDA label 'stru_14C3851A0' is the object's real label. The 4-byte dword at 0x14C385198 that IDA also calls g_onlineMgr is used only by Online_MatchData_Load@0x14104F9F3 (write), G_SaveMP_ReadMainStateDword@0x14104FA27 (write), Online_MatchData_RecordBreadcrumbCount@0x14104FB97 (read) and G_SaveMP_WriteMainStateField@0x14104FD24 (read); it is not OnlineMgr state and needs its own name (not proposed here: no name is proven).

renames: the object's own label; dynamic_initializer_for_g_onlineMgr@0x140346CA0 and dynamic_initializer_for_g_onlineMgr_dataChannelsAndLogin@0x140340670 initialize this address and dynamic_atexit_destructor_for_g_onlineMgr@0x142349640 destroys it
